failures.title: Peugeot DV5RC Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue System Issues - NOx Sensors, Injectors & Heater Units
items.whatHappens: The DV5RC uses an AdBlue (Selective Catalytic Reduction) system to meet Euro 6d emissions standards. The system is complex and prone to issues: NOx sensors can fail, the AdBlue injector can clog, and the heated AdBlue line can fail in cold weather. When the system detects a fault, it triggers a countdown that can limit vehicle speed and eventually prevent starting. This is one of the most common sources of frustration for owners of BlueHDi-equipped vehicles.
items.repairVsReplace: Sensor and injector replacement is a specialist job (£300-£800 per component). Heated line replacement can cost £200-£500. These are repairable issues and rarely require engine replacement, though they can be expensive to diagnose and fix. Read our full AdBlue system failure guide

items.title: DPF & EGR Clogging - Urban Driving Issues
items.whatHappens: Like all modern diesels, the DV5RC's Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) and Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) system are prone to clogging, particularly on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys where the DPF cannot complete a regeneration cycle. Symptoms include reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and warning lights.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning is a specialist job (£200-£600). EGR valve cleaning or replacement is also manageable (£200-£500). These are repairable issues and rarely require engine replacement. Read our full DPF failure guide

items.title: Timing Chain & Injector Wear - High-Mileage Issues
items.whatHappens: The DV5RC uses a timing chain that can stretch over time, particularly on high-mileage examples or those with extended oil change intervals. Fuel injectors can also wear or become clogged, causing misfires, rough running, and starting issues.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement is a specialist job (£800-£1,500). Injector replacement is also manageable (£200-£500 per injector). Neither typically requires engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The DV5RC was introduced in 2018 as an updated and more refined version of the 1.6 HDi. Post-2020 engines benefit from improved AdBlue system components and software updates that reduce the frequency of sensor failures. However, the DPF and EGR issues are inherent to all modern diesels with urban use - regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration is essential. Using the correct oil (PSA B71 2312) and fuel additives can help extend component life.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the DV5RC
variants.intro: The DV5RC is the 130 hp version of the 1.5-litre BlueHDi engine family. It's part of the DV5 family, which also includes the DV5RE (120 hp, with AdBlue) and various other tuning levels for commercial and passenger applications. The DV5RC is distinguished by its 130 hp output, specific ECU calibration, and its widespread use across the Stellantis range. Where the code appears: - Stamped on a metal plate on the engine block (left-hand side, near the timing cover) - On the V5C logbook under "Engine number" (the first 6 characters will read DV5RC) - Via VIN decoder - the BlueHDi family is identified by the model designation Commonly confused with: - DV5RE - 120 hp lower-output version, different ECU calibration, sometimes without AdBlue depending on market - DV6TED4 - 1.6 HDi (110-120 hp), the predecessor engine; completely different block and architecture - [DV10 - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - 2.0-litre BlueHDi, larger capacity and higher torque, not interchangeable

relatives.description: - the 1.6‑litre HDi diesel that preceded the DV5 family in the Peugeot 208, 308 and Citroën C4. Known for injector failure and DPF clogging - the DV5RC replaced it with improved emissions technology and increased refinement, but introduced its own AdBlue system complexities.

DV5RC (updated versions) / - the 120 hp lower‑output version of the 1.5 BlueHDi. The DV5RC itself has been updated over time with improved AdBlue system components and revised software. From 2024 onwards, Stellantis has been transitioning away from pure diesel in passenger cars, with electrified options replacing the BlueHDi range.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement DV5RC - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used DV5RC can make sense for lower-value Peugeot 208 or Citroën C3 models where the car's value doesn't justify a recon unit. However, the AdBlue system and DPF are the biggest risks - only consider a used unit with documented proof of recent AdBlue system service and DPF cleaning. The timing chain is also a potential issue on higher-mileage examples. Without a documented history, factor in £1,000-£2,000 for preventative work (AdBlue service, DPF cleaning, chain inspection). Link once: /services/used-engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper DV5RC recon is the best option for owners planning to keep their car long-term, especially for the heavier 3008, 5008 and C5 Aircross where the engine works harder. A quality recon should include: full strip and inspection, new timing chain and guides (critical), new injectors, new DPF or full cleaning, AdBlue system inspection/refurbishment, new gaskets and seals, and a full test. With a 12-24 month warranty, this gives you peace of mind that the engine's known weaknesses have been addressed - well worth the £1,200-£2,200 supply cost. Link once: /services/reconditioned-engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified when the original engine has suffered catastrophic failure (timing chain failure with valve damage, severe injector failure causing cylinder wash) and the car is a cherished keeper or low-mileage example. An upgraded rebuild should include new crankshaft bearings, conrod bearings, new pistons/rings if damaged, refreshed cylinder head, and a full AdBlue/DPF system overhaul. This is specialist territory and typically only makes sense for cars with strong residual value. Link once: /services/rebuilt-engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted Peugeot diesel specialists nationwide, with 12-month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units. Link once: /services/supply-and-fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The DV5RC sits in Peugeot 208, 308, 2008, 3008, 5008, Citroën C3, C4, C5 Aircross and other Stellantis models - cars worth £6,000-£30,000 depending on age and condition. With a reconditioned supply cost of £1,200-£2,200, replacement is viable on most examples. However, for a sub-£4,000 208 or C3 with high mileage and a failed engine, a used unit (£600-£1,200) with documented history may be the only sensible option. For cars worth under £3,000, consider breaking the car before committing to a replacement engine. For heavier vehicles like the 3008 and 5008 where the DV5RC is a popular choice, a reconditioned unit is strongly recommended to ensure longevity and reliability.

items.question: What are the most common failures on the DV5RC BlueHDi engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are AdBlue system failures (NOx sensors, injector clogging, heated line failure), DPF and EGR clogging (particularly with urban driving), and timing chain wear on higher-mileage examples. The AdBlue system is the most common source of frustration for owners, often triggering countdown warnings and speed limitations. AdBlue system: sensor and injector replacement is the most common repair. DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving is essential for regeneration. Timing chain: preventative replacement recommended at 60k-80k miles.

DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving is essential for regeneration.

items.question: Which models use the DV5RC 1.5 BlueHDi engine?
items.answer: The DV5RC is fitted to a wide range of Stellantis models: Peugeot 208 (II), 308 (II & III), 2008 (II), 3008 (II), 5008 (II), 508 (II), Partner (III), Citroën C3 (III), C4 (III), C5 Aircross, Berlingo (III), DS 3 Crossback, DS 4, DS 7 Crossback, and Opel/Vauxhall Astra L, Corsa F, Mokka B and Grandland. Not to be confused with the DV5RE (120 hp lower-output version). Not to be confused with the older DV6TED4 1.6 HDi.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned DV5RC engine?
items.answer: A used DV5RC can be viable for lower-value Peugeot 208 or Citroën C3 models, but only if it has documented proof of recent AdBlue system service, DPF cleaning, and timing chain inspection. Without that, factor in £1,000-£2,000 for preventative work. A reconditioned engine is the safer choice - it includes new timing chain, injectors, DPF cleaning, and AdBlue system inspection, with a 12-24 month warranty. Used is cheaper (£600-£1,200) but AdBlue and DPF risks are significant. Reconditioned addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.

Reconditioned: addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.

items.question: How do I confirm if my car has the DV5RC or the DV5RE?
items.answer: Check the engine code stamped on the block (left-hand side near the timing cover) - it will read DV5RC for the 130 hp variant, or DV5RE for the 120 hp variant. The V5C logbook also lists the full engine number, with the first 6 characters identifying the code. DV5RC: 130 hp, specific ECU calibration, used in most passenger cars. DV5RE: 120 hp, different ECU calibration, sometimes without AdBlue. Fitting the wrong variant requires ECU reflash - not a straight swap.

items.question: How long does a DV5RC engine typically last?
items.answer: With meticulous maintenance and early preventative work, these engines can exceed 120,000-150,000 miles. The DV5RC is fundamentally a good engine; the limiting factors are the AdBlue system, DPF/EGR, and timing chain wear. AdBlue system: regular servicing and use of quality AdBlue is essential. DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving (20+ minutes) for DPF regeneration. Timing chain: preventative inspection at 60k-80k miles.
